student_notes: Questions from production engineer review. Focus on practical application.

questions.question: clarify_node explicitly calls update_session_state() before returning when it short-circuits the pipeline. Why? What breaks if you remove that call?
options: A. The bot_response won't be emitted to the client
B. The LangSmith trace won't capture the clarification event
C. Filter updates from filter_apply_node (e.g., city='Bangalore' was already known) will be lost because followup_node never runs
D. The A/B experiment assignment won't be persisted
questions.explanation: The pipeline is linear: filter_apply_node runs BEFORE clarify_node. If a user says 'show me something affordable in Bangalore' — city=Bangalore gets merged into active_filters in filter_apply_node, then clarify_node short-circuits to ask about budget. Without explicit session persistence in clarify_node, the city filter is in memory but never written to Redis. On the next turn (when user answers the budget question), make_base_state loads the old session from Redis — city is gone, the user has to specify it again. This is a subtle but production-breaking bug.

questions.question: The route_node has a tier system from 0 to 3b. A new intent 'schedule_site_visit' needs to: authenticate the user, call a booking API, and return a confirmation. Describe which tier this belongs to and precisely what route_node should do for it.
questions.answer: This is Tier 1 with requires_auth=True. route_node first checks requires_auth — since no auth_token exists in the session, it short-circuits to build_login_template_response() before tier routing. Once authenticated, on the next turn route_node sees auth_token present and routes to Tier 1: execute_tier1_action() calls the booking API and returns a confirmation template. No LLM is involved. The key point: auth check happens before tier routing, not inside the tier 1 executor.
questions.explanation: The requires_auth check is a pre-routing gate. This design means you never accidentally execute a Tier 1 action for an unauthenticated user — the check is in one place (route_node), not scattered across tier executors.

questions.question: A user says 'tell me more about the second property' after a carousel has been shown. Which node resolves 'second' to an actual property_id and how?
options: A. classify_node — the SLM resolves ordinal references during classification
B. resolve_entities_node — it reads entity_refs from the classification and looks up carousel_state.items[1]
C. fetch_data_node — it fetches the property_id from the Housing API using 'second' as a search term
D. llm_node — the LLM resolves ordinal references using its built-in world knowledge
questions.explanation: resolve_entities_node processes entity_refs (the SLM outputs entity_refs: [{looking_for: 'property', by: 'cardinality', value: 2}]). It looks up carousel_state.items[1] (0-indexed), gets the property_id, and stores it in session.active_property_id. The LLM never sees carousel items directly — the orchestrator resolves the reference and injects the property context into the system prompt. This keeps LLM token cost near zero for reference resolution.
